user.title: Welcome to Hestia Weather
user.description:
Hestia Weather is the brain of the weather at home: it reads your forecast, your station and the air quality, then works out what they mean.

Four steps, each already filled with what Home Assistant knows:
1. **Weather**: the forecast source.
2. **Station**: your sensors, if any.
3. **Air and pollen**: optional.
4. **Sensors**: what you want for your automations.

Everything can be changed later in **Configure**.

menu_options.import_card: Start from a Hestia Weather card’s settings

import_card.title: Start from a card
import_card.description: Choose the card. Its settings are shown at each step, to check them.

weather.title: Step 1 of 4 · Weather
weather.description: The forecast source and the name of the place.

data_description.location: Shown at the top of the card.
data_description.vigilance_entity: Optional: Météo-France or MeteoSwiss (aggregate warnings sensor).
data_description.season_entity: Optional. Without a sensor, the season follows the date.
data_description.water_restriction_entity: Optional: the alert level of the Vigieau integration, drinking water zone (AEP).
data_description.lightning_entity: Optional: the distance sensor of the Blitzortung integration. Within 30 km, the Storm sensor turns on.

data_description.station_history: Rain totals, temperature trend and the day’s strongest gust, when the station does not provide them.

station_sensors.title: Step 2 of 4 · Station sensors
station_sensors.description: Check each sensor. Leave empty what the station does not measure.

pollen_sensors.title: Step 3 of 4 · {source} sensors
pollen_sensors.description: The species to follow (and, for Polleninformation, the overall allergy risk), proposed by Hestia: check, add or remove. Without an overall risk, Hestia keeps the highest species.

data_description.pollen_risk_entity: Optional. Without it, Hestia uses the highest species.

families.title: Step 4 of 4 · Sensors and automations
families.description: Tick what you want to use. The entities of these families will be enabled when their source is there. Each one can be changed later in **Configure**.

summary.title: Summary

air_quality.title: Step 3 of 4 · Air quality
air_quality.description:
The air index from 1 to 6 and its pollutants.

- **Atmo France**: your town’s forecast.
- **WAQI**: the chosen station’s measure; tomorrow comes from Open-Meteo’s forecast (Copernicus), at the home’s position.

« None »: no air quality.{hint}

pollen.title: Step 3 of 4 · Pollen
pollen.description: Choose a source for the countries it covers. Atmo France uses an index from 1 to 6; Polleninformation, IRM KMI and Swiss Pollen use levels from 0 to 4; Kleenex / Scottex uses levels from 1 to 4. With Swiss Pollen or Kleenex / Scottex, choose one station or location, then the species or groups to follow.

pollen_area.title: Step 3 of 4 · Atmo zone for pollen
pollen_area.description: The Atmo France zone whose pollen Hestia reads. It can differ from the air quality zone.

pollen_station.title: Pollen location
pollen_station.description: Choose one station or location for the species and groups to follow.

error.polleninformation_missing: Polleninformation is not installed. Install the Polleninformation EU integration (github.com/krissen/polleninformation), then come back.
error.irm_kmi_missing: IRM KMI is not installed, or gives no pollen. Install the IRM KMI integration from HACS (github.com/jdejaegh/irm-kmi-ha), then come back.
error.swiss_pollen_missing: Swiss Pollen is not installed or provides no level sensors. Install frimtec/hass-swiss-pollen through HACS, then return here.
error.swiss_station_missing: Choose an available station or location for this pollen source.
error.kleenex_pollenradar_missing: Kleenex / Scottex is not installed or provides no pollen sensors. Install Kleenex Pollen Radar from HACS, then return here.
